subject: Qur'an & Tajweed
source: Continues the school Drive Quran folder progression (TPS Quran Tracker tajweed rules Years 1-6) into KS3/KS4; classical tajweed (Hafs 'an 'Asim) and tadabbur method; Qur'an text per the Madinah mushaf

lessons.unit: Unit 1: Noon and meem - complete rules
lessons.title: Diagnostic: noon, meem and madd
objectives: Show recall of rules from KS2 and Year 7
Identify gaps with a diagnostic quiz
Plan targeted practice

keywords.def: a check to find what you know and what to improve

starter: Bismillah. Recite the isti'adha and basmalah.
Name the four rules of noon sakinah and tanween with letters.
Name the types of madd lazim.

teach.heading: Why diagnose?
bullets: Recitation is a skill built over years
teach.note: Explain that Year 8 builds on all earlier learning. Ask: what has been your most secure rule? Which is least secure? Pupils note answers privately.

teach.heading: Quiz
teach.note: Run the quiz in a form or on paper. Questions include: which rule in مِن بَعْدِ? How many counts for الضَّالِّينَ? Tell pupils the purpose is learning, not marks.

teach.heading: Recite and spot
bullets: Mark each rule on a printed copy
teach.note: Pupils mark a printed Al-Fatihah with every rule. Check: the yaa in إِيَّاكَ carries a shaddah but no ghunnah, since ghunnah belongs to noon and meem. Discuss errors kindly and clarify.

teach.heading: Targets
bullets: Choose a surah to practise on
teach.note: Pupils write targets and a plan. Share a few. Close with a dua for steadfastness in learning the Qur'an.

practice: Which rule is in مِن بَعْدِ?
How many counts for madd lazim?
independent: Complete the diagnostic quiz
Mark the rules on Al-Fatihah
Write two targets and a plan
exit: Name one rule you are secure with.
What will you practise this week?
lessons.homework: Practise your two target rules daily with five examples each.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: quiz with word bank and examples. Stretch: write extra quiz questions for the class.

lessons.title: Noon sakinah and tanween in depth
lessons.bigQuestion: Why do you think the same 'n' sound changes in four different ways? What would recitation sound like without these rules?
objectives: To understand the four rules of noon sakinah and tanween in full, including the exceptions, and apply them in Al-Haqqah
successCriteria: All: classify any noon sakinah or tanween by its next letter
Most: explain the ghunnah in idgham, iqlab and ikhfa
Some: explain izhar mutlaq in words like ٱلدُّنْيَا
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: tajweed as care and respect for Allah's words

keywords.def: a double vowel ending with an n sound
a clear noon before ي or و in one word
a nasal sound held for two counts

hook.text: Why do you think the same 'n' sound changes in four different ways? What would recitation sound like without these rules?
hook.a: The rules make the flow easy and beautiful; without them recitation would be choppy, and they are how the Qur'an was recited to the Prophet ﷺ.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'And recite the Qur'an with measured recitation (tartil)' (Al-Muzzammil 73:4).

starter.q: Which surahs are Year 8's first targets?

teach.heading: The four rules at a glance
teach.note: Bismillah. Placement (induction week) showed where each group is; this recaps the full system.

head: Rule
Letters
Ghunnah
Example
rows: ء ه ع ح غ خ

teach.heading: Exceptions to know
bullets: Izhar mutlaq: noon and ي/و in one word
teach.note: These four words (دنيا, بنيان, صنوان, قنوان) keep the noon clear so the meaning is not confused with a doubled letter.

teach.heading: Levels of ikhfa
bullets: Near ط ض ص ظ ق ك: heavier hum
Near ت د ث: lighter hum
Prepare the tongue for the next letter
teach.note: Ikhfa is coloured by the next letter. Model مِنكُم (69:18) and وَمَن قَبْلَهُۥ (69:9).

teach.heading: Common mistake
teach.note: Pupils often add a clear noon in ikhfa.

misconception.wrong: minkum: a clear noon pressed on the gum
misconception.right: min-kum: tongue does not touch for noon; hum from the nose, then ك

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: Launch the Teams poll. Read the results, then explain the right answer.

check.why: Tanween before ب is always iqlab; the small meem in the mushaf shows it.

practice.q: Classify every noon sakinah and tanween in 69:6 to 7.
practice.a: عَادٌۭ فَأُهْلِكُوا۟ ikhfa; بِرِيحٍۢ صَرْصَرٍ ikhfa; صَرْصَرٍ عَاتِيَةٍۢ izhar; لَيَالٍۢ وَثَمَٰنِيَةَ idgham with ghunnah; أَيَّامٍ حُسُومًۭا izhar; حُسُومًۭا فَتَرَى ikhfa; نَخْلٍ خَاوِيَةٍۢ izhar.
practice.model: I do: 69:6 عَادٌۭ then ف: ikhfa. بِرِيحٍۢ then ص: ikhfa (heavier hum). صَرْصَرٍ then ع: izhar, clear.

independent.q: Rule audit (pupil PDF): classify the noon sakinah and tanween in Al-Haqqah 69:40 to 52. Today's rota group recites Al-Mulk 67:1 to 10.
independent.a: رَسُولٍۢ كَرِيمٍۢ ikhfa; شَاعِرٍۢ قَلِيلًۭا ikhfa; قَلِيلًۭا مَّا idgham; تَنزِيلٌۭ ikhfa (in word) and مِّن idgham; مِّن رَّبِّ idgham no ghunnah; مِنْهُ izhar; مِنكُم ikhfa; مِّنْ أَحَدٍ izhar; أَحَدٍ عَنْهُ izhar; لَتَذْكِرَةٌۭ لِّلْمُتَّقِينَ idgham no ghunnah; لَحَسْرَةٌ عَلَى izhar.
independent.model: The teacher does 69:40: رَسُولٍۢ كَرِيمٍۢ: tanween before ك: ikhfa.

independent.q: Extend: give the four izhar mutlaq words.
independent.a: ٱلدُّنْيَا, صِنْوَانٌ, قِنْوَانٌ, بُنْيَٰنٌ

independent.q: Stretch: why is ikhfa before ق heavier than before ت?
independent.a: The hum takes the colour of the next letter; ق is a heavy (isti'la) letter.

exit.a: idgham without ghunnah

exit.q: Back to our ponder: Why do you think the same 'n' sound changes in four different ways? What would recitation sound like without these rules?
exit.a: The rules make the flow easy and beautiful; without them recitation would be choppy, and they are how the Qur'an was recited to the Prophet ﷺ.

lessons.unit: Spring 1: Al-Haqqah; noon and meem recap and when letters meet
lessons.title: Meem sakinah and ghunnah in detail
lessons.bigQuestion: Your lips make both م and ب. What do you think happens when a meem sakinah meets a baa?
objectives: To understand the three rules of meem sakinah and the ghunnah of noon and meem with shaddah, and apply them accurately
successCriteria: All: name the three meem sakinah rules
Most: read ikhfa shafawi with lips lightly closed
Some: explain why care is needed before و and ف
lessons.smsc: Cultural: the oral chain (isnad) of recitation passing these rules from teacher to pupil

keywords.def: a nasal sound held for two counts

hook.text: Your lips make both م and ب. What do you think happens when a meem sakinah meets a baa?
hook.a: The meem is hidden with a two-count hum, lips lightly together: ikhfa shafawi.

islamicLink.text: The Prophet ﷺ said: 'The one who is skilled in the Qur'an will be with the noble and righteous scribes' (Bukhari and Muslim).

starter.q: Recite Al-Haqqah 69:3 in your head. How does the next ayah begin?

teach.heading: Three rules of meem sakinah
teach.note: Bismillah. Shafawi means 'of the lips'.

teach.heading: Extra care: و and ف
bullets: Izhar shafawi is strongest before و and ف
Same lips, so meem may slip into them
Close fully for م, then open
teach.note: Model عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا (1:7) and لَهُمْ فِيهَا.

teach.heading: Ghunnah with shaddah
bullets: نّ and مّ: always two counts

teach.heading: Common mistake
teach.note: Pressing the lips too hard in ikhfa shafawi.

misconception.wrong: fabash-shirhum-m-m bi'adhaab: lips pressed shut, a full meem
misconception.right: Lips touch lightly, a gentle two-count hum, then ب

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: Launch the Teams poll. Read the results, then explain the right answer.

check.why: Meem sakinah before meem merges with ghunnah: idgham shafawi (mithlayn saghir).

practice.q: Read 69:7 to 8 and name every meem sakinah rule and ghunnah.
practice.a: سَخَّرَهَا عَلَيْهِمْ سَبْعَ izhar shafawi; كَأَنَّهُمْ أَعْجَازُ izhar shafawi and ghunnah on نّ; لَهُم مِّنۢ idgham shafawi.
practice.model: I do: عَلَيْهِمْ then س: izhar shafawi, close the lips and open. كَأَنَّهُمْ: نّ has a two-count ghunnah; then هُمْ before أ: izhar shafawi.

independent.q: Meem audit (pupil PDF): classify each meem sakinah in 69:18 to 30. Today's rota group recites Al-Qalam 68:1 to 16.
independent.a: مِنكُمْ خَافِيَةٌۭ (69:18), لَمْ أُوتَ (69:25), وَلَمْ أَدْرِ (69:26): all izhar shafawi. (هَآؤُمُ in 69:19 has a vowel, so no rule.)
independent.model: The teacher does 69:18: مِنكُمْ خَافِيَةٌۭ: meem sakinah before خ: izhar shafawi.

independent.q: Extend: find one idgham shafawi in Al-Mulk or Al-Qalam.
Stretch: explain why ikhfa shafawi has ghunnah but izhar shafawi does not.
independent.a: Before ب the meem is hidden, so its natural ghunnah shows; before other letters it is said clearly and complete.

exit.a: ikhfa shafawi

exit.q: Back to our ponder: Your lips make both م and ب. What do you think happens when a meem sakinah meets a baa?
exit.a: The meem is hidden with a two-count hum, lips lightly together: ikhfa shafawi.

lessons.unit: Spring 1: Al-Haqqah; noon and meem recap and when letters meet
lessons.title: When letters meet: identical, close and same-place letters
lessons.bigQuestion: When two people with the same name meet, how do we keep them apart? What happens when two identical letters meet?
objectives: To understand how letters that meet merge or stay clear (mithlayn, mutajanisayn, mutaqaribayn) and recite them correctly
successCriteria: All: define mithlayn, mutajanisayn and mutaqaribayn
Most: read the common idgham pairs correctly
Some: explain the saktah in مَالِيَهْ ۜ هَلَكَ (69:28 to 29)
lessons.smsc: Cultural: the precision of the Hafs recitation passed down teacher to pupil

keywords.def: a short silent pause without breath

hook.text: When two people with the same name meet, how do we keep them apart? What happens when two identical letters meet?
hook.a: Identical letters usually merge into one with a shaddah (mithlayn): ٱضْرِب بِّعَصَاكَ.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'Those to whom We have given the Book recite it with its true recital' (Al-Baqarah 2:121).

starter.q: Recite Al-Haqqah 69:9 in your head. How does the next ayah begin?
Which letters share ط د ت's makhraj?

teach.heading: Three relationships
teach.note: Bismillah. Saghir: the first letter has sukoon and the second a vowel; then idgham happens in these cases.

teach.heading: Same-place pairs that merge
teach.note: Read each slowly.

teach.heading: When they do not merge
bullets: A madd letter: فِى يَوْمٍ stays apart
Ikhfa or izhar rules where they apply
teach.note: In 69:28 to 29 the mushaf shows ۜ: Hafs reads with a short silent pause (saktah) so the two haas stay apart; idgham is also narrated, but the pause is what we teach.

misconception.wrong: qad tabayyana: a clear daal, then taa
misconception.right: qat-tabayyana: the daal merges fully into the taa

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: Launch the Teams poll. Read the results, then explain the right answer.

check.why: ت and ط share a makhraj but differ in sifat, so mutajanisayn; the ت merges into ط.

practice.q: Read «يَلْهَث ذَّٰلِكَ» (7:176) and «وَقُل رَّبِّ» (17:24): name the meeting and how to read it.
practice.a: ث into ذ: mutajanisayn, yalhadh-dhaalik. ل into ر: mutaqaribayn, wa qur-rabbi.
practice.model: I do: يَلْهَث ذَّٰلِكَ: ث and ذ both come from the tongue tip with the edge of the top teeth, so same makhraj: mutajanisayn. The ث disappears into the ذ, which has a shaddah.

independent.q: Meeting-letters sort (pupil PDF): sort 9 examples into mithlayn, mutajanisayn, mutaqaribayn. Today's rota group recites 69:1 to 12.
independent.a: Mithlayn: ٱضْرِب بِّعَصَاكَ, عَلَيْهِم مُّؤْصَدَةٌ, رَبِحَت تِّجَٰرَتُهُمْ. Mutajanisayn: قَد تَّبَيَّنَ, قَالَت طَّآئِفَةٌ, إِذ ظَّلَمُوٓا۟. Mutaqaribayn: وَقُل رَّبِّ, نَخْلُقكُّم, and laam of al- before sun letters.
independent.model: The teacher sorts the first: ٱضْرِب بِّعَصَاكَ: ب and ب, identical: mithlayn.

independent.q: Extend: find one mithlayn in Al-Mulk or Al-Qalam.
independent.a: Pupil gives an example (e.g. meem into meem) checked by the teacher.

independent.q: Stretch: why does the laam of al- merge into sun letters?
independent.a: Laam and the sun letters are close in makhraj (mutaqaribayn), so it merges.

exit.q: ق into ك in «نَخْلُقكُّم» (77:20) is ...
exit.a: mutaqaribayn

exit.q: Back to our ponder: When two people with the same name meet, how do we keep them apart? What happens when two identical letters meet?
exit.a: Identical letters usually merge into one with a shaddah (mithlayn): ٱضْرِب بِّعَصَاكَ.

lessons.unit: Unit 3: Stopping and starting well
lessons.title: Waqf and ibtida': four types of stop
objectives: Define waqf and ibtida'
Name the four types of waqf
Choose good places to stop and start

keywords.def: a complete stop - the meaning is finished
a sufficient stop - connected in meaning
a good stop, but start again from earlier
a poor stop which spoils the meaning

starter: Name the stopping signs in the mushaf.
How do you stop on a word with ة?

teach.heading: Why stopping matters
bullets: Stopping in the wrong place can change meaning
The Qur'an is clear and we protect it
Scholars set out rules for stopping
teach.note: Introduce with the example of stopping at لَا تَقْرَبُوا الصَّلَاةَ (4:43) before وَأَنتُمْ سُكَارَىٰ: the meaning would be 'do not approach the prayer', which is wrong. Pupils explain why it is a poor stop.

teach.heading: Four types
teach.note: Give a simple explanation of each. Tamm: no link to what follows. Kafi: connected in meaning but separate grammatically. Hasan: sentence is fine but connected to what follows. Qabih: breaks the meaning.

teach.heading: Starting again
bullets: Begin where the meaning is sound
Do not begin on half a word
teach.note: If you run out of breath at a poor place, go back to a good starting place. Model with a long ayah. Pupils practise with Al-Ma'un.

teach.heading: Using the signs
bullets: Follow signs in the Madinah mushaf
Take a breath at ayah ends
teach.note: Pupils read a page with signs. Teacher checks. Mention that stopping at the end of an ayah is the preferred practice for beginners.

practice: Why is stopping at لَا تَقْرَبُوا الصَّلَاةَ a poor stop?
independent: Mark stops on a printed Al-Ma'un
Classify four stops as good or poor with reasons
Recite a passage with correct waqf
exit: Name the four types of waqf.
What should you do if you run out of breath at a poor place?
lessons.homework: Read a page of the mushaf with correct stops and breaths.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: sign flash cards and examples. Stretch: explain why starting matters as much as stopping.

lessons.unit: Unit 3: Stopping and starting well
lessons.title: Waqf in practice: stopping on different endings
objectives: Stop correctly on all endings
Know that roum and ishmam exist and are learned with a teacher
Recite a long ayah with good breath
starter: How do we stop on tanween fathah?
How do we stop on round ة?

teach.heading: Rules for stopping
bullets: Tanween kasrah or dammah: drop it
teach.note: Model each. Examples: رَحِيمًا to 'raheema'; أَحَدٌ to 'ahad'; الْمِسْكِينِ unchanged; رَحْمَةٌ to 'rahmah'. Pupils practise on words from the mushaf.

teach.heading: With madd
teach.note: Revise madd 'arid. Pupils recite the end of each ayah of Al-Fatihah with 4 counts. Explain that the choice of length is your teacher's guidance.

teach.heading: Echo and heavy letters
bullets: Stopping on heavy letters: keep full
teach.note: Pupils practise the echo on stopped words. Heavy letters at the end keep their fullness. Do not add a vowel. Pairs give feedback.

teach.heading: Long ayat
bullets: Look ahead to find a breath point
teach.note: Use Al-Ma'un as a practice text. Where can we breathe in ayat 5-7? Choose points that suit the meaning. Teacher gives guidance.

practice: How do you stop on تَوَّابًا?
What happens to ة when stopping?
independent: Write the stopped form of 10 words
Recite Al-Fatihah stopping at every ayah
Mark breath points on Al-Ma'un
exit: How do you stop on a word with tanween kasrah?
What do we do with madd when stopping?
lessons.homework: Record yourself stopping at each ayah of a surah you know and listen for errors.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: table with stopped forms. Stretch: explain how stopping affects qalqalah.

lessons.unit: Unit 4: Surah study - Al-Ma'un and At-Takathur
lessons.title: Surat Al-Ma'un: reading and rules
objectives: Recite Al-Ma'un accurately
Apply tajweed rules
Understand the meaning
starter: Name the four types of waqf.
Which rule is used for tanween before laam?

teach.heading: Ayat 1-3
teach.note: Meaning: Have you seen the one who denies the judgement? That is the one who pushes away the orphan and does not urge the feeding of the poor. Chunk and echo.

teach.heading: Ayat 4-7
teach.note: Meaning: so woe to those who pray, who are heedless of their prayer, who show off, and who withhold small kindnesses. Chunk and echo. Explain that the prayer must be sincere and joined with kindness.

teach.heading: Tajweed
bullets: عَن صَلَاتِهِمْ - ikhfa with heavy Saad
teach.note: Pupils label each. Notice the heavy Saad after ikhfa. Check the natural madd in سَاهُونَ and مَاعُونَ. Compare ayat 5 and 6, which start the same.

teach.heading: Memorise
teach.note: Use chaining and link the repeated phrase الَّذِينَ هُمْ. Test aloud with a partner. Assess with the rubric.

practice: Which rule is in فَوَيْلٌ لِّلْمُصَلِّينَ?
independent: Label tajweed rules on a printed Al-Ma'un
Memorise ayat 1-3
Recite individually
exit: What does ayah 3 tell us to do?
lessons.homework: Recite Al-Ma'un daily and learn ayat 1-3 by heart.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: chunked audio and translation. Stretch: learn the whole surah.

lessons.unit: Unit 4: Surah study - Al-Ma'un and At-Takathur
lessons.title: Surat Al-Ma'un: tadabbur
objectives: Explain the main themes of Al-Ma'un
Use the four questions method for tadabbur
Connect belief and character

teach.heading: Belief and kindness
bullets: Denying the judgement leads to harshness
teach.note: Discuss the link between ayah 1 and ayat 2-3. The surah connects belief in the Day of Judgement with the treatment of orphans and the poor. Ask: how does belief change behaviour?

teach.heading: Sincere prayer
bullets: Allah wants prayer with focus and sincerity
teach.note: Explain gently: the surah warns against heedlessness and showing off. We should check our intentions. Ask: how can we pray with focus?

teach.heading: Small kindnesses
teach.note: Scholars mention that al-ma'un includes small items of everyday help. Pupils give examples: lending a pencil, holding a door, giving a tissue. Ask: which can you do tomorrow?

teach.heading: Action plan
teach.note: Pupils write an action plan: what, when, and for whom. Share some. Close with a dua asking Allah to make us sincere.

practice: Why does the surah mention the orphan and the poor?
independent: Answer the four tadabbur questions on ayat 1-3
Write an action plan with three kindnesses
Recite Al-Ma'un to a partner
exit: Name one theme of the surah.
What will you do this week?
lessons.homework: Do one small kindness each day this week and record it.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: sentence frames for reflection. Stretch: write a short essay on belief and behaviour.

lessons.unit: Unit 4: Surah study - Al-Ma'un and At-Takathur
lessons.title: Surat At-Takathur: reading and rules
objectives: Recite At-Takathur accurately
Apply tajweed rules
Understand its warning

teach.heading: Ayat 1-4
teach.note: Meaning: competing for more distracts you until you visit the graves. No! You will know. Again, no! You will know. Chunk and echo. Note ghunnah on ثُمَّ.

teach.heading: Ayat 5-8
teach.note: Meaning: if you knew with certainty, you would surely see the Hellfire, then you will see it with certain sight, then you will be asked about the blessings. Present the surah as a gentle wake-up call, not a threat.

teach.heading: Tajweed
teach.note: Pupils label rules. The laam of التَّكَاثُرُ merges into the taa. The noon with shaddah in لَتَرَوُنَّ is ghunnah. Practise the madd letters and counts.

teach.heading: Memorise
teach.note: Use chaining and link patterns. Note the repeated كَلَّا and ثُمَّ. Test in pairs and give feedback using the rubric.

practice: Where is ghunnah in the surah?
independent: Label rules in At-Takathur
Memorise ayat 1-4
Recite individually
lessons.homework: Recite At-Takathur daily and learn ayat 1-4 by heart.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: chunked audio and translation. Stretch: learn the whole surah.

lessons.unit: Unit 4: Surah study - Al-Ma'un and At-Takathur
lessons.title: At-Takathur: tadabbur and gratitude
objectives: Explain the lesson of At-Takathur
Link it to gratitude (shukr)
Recite the whole surah

teach.heading: Competing for more

hook.text: Al-Haqqah means 'the Inevitable Reality'. Why might the surah begin by asking three times what it is?

head: Ayah
Translation of the meaning (Saheeh International)
rows: The Inevitable Reality - What is the Inevitable Reality?
And what can make you know what is the Inevitable Reality? Thamud and 'Aad denied the Striking Calamity.
So as for Thamud, they were destroyed by the overpowering [blast]. And as for 'Aad, they were destroyed by a screaming, violent wind

Which Allah imposed upon them for seven nights and eight days in succession, so you would see the people therein fallen as if they were hollow trunks of palm trees. Then do you see of them any remains?
And there came Pharaoh and those before him and the overturned cities with sin. And they disobeyed the messenger of their Lord, so He seized them with a seizure exceeding [in severity].
Indeed, when the water overflowed, We carried your ancestors in the sailing ship That We might make it for you a reminder and [that] a conscious ear would be conscious of it.
